name: Hochgurgl
kurzbeschreibung: High-altitude Hochgurgl (2,150 m) boasts snow security, the Top Mountain Crosspoint museum, and entry to the Timmelsjoch pass road.
dauer: 2 to 4 hours (half-day excursion in combination with Timmelsjoch)
preis: Motorcycle museum adults approx. €15.00; Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road subject to separate toll
oeffnungszeiten: Museum and restaurant in summer daily 09:00 to 18:00; winter operations November to May
beschreibung:
Overview

The prestigious high-altitude resort of Hochgurgl perches at a snow-reliable 2,150 meters above sea level above Obergurgl in the rear Ötztal, ranking among the highest hotel settlements in the entire Alps. Together, Obergurgl and Hochgurgl form the exclusive "Gurgl – Diamond of the Alps" ski area, ensuring reliable snow cover from mid-November to early May across expansive pistes. In summer, Hochgurgl becomes the gateway to the world-famous Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road, which climbs over the 2,509-meter mountain pass into South Tyrol. The architectural and cultural focal point of the settlement is the futuristic "Top Mountain Crosspoint" complex: it combines the modern Kirchenkarbahn gondola, a panoramic restaurant, the toll station, and Europe's highest motorcycle museum beneath an elegant curved timber roof.

Route & Requirements

Hochgurgl serves as an ideal base for gentle scenic walks as well as demanding high-alpine summit tours. From the mountain stations of Kirchenkarbahn I and II at over 2,800 meters, panoramic ridgeways offer breathtaking vistas down the Ötztal and into the Stubai Alps. Visiting the motorcycle museum inside the Top Mountain Crosspoint – displaying over 500 historic motorcycles and classic motorcars – is completely barrier-free and weather-independent. For hiking in the alpine terrain surrounding Hochgurgl, ankle-high hiking boots with grippy soles, windproof outerwear, and sun protection are essential, as alpine weather can shift rapidly. Experienced mountaineers can tackle the ridge scramble to Schermerspitze. Casual walkers can enjoy flat gravel paths around the resort, savoring the clean, allergen-free mountain air.

Visit & Arrival

The Top Mountain Motorcycle Museum and restaurant are open daily in summer from late May to late October from 09:00 to 18:00, and throughout the winter season. Motorists reach Hochgurgl toll-free from Germany via the A7 and Fernpass or via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Ötztal), following the B186 for 50 kilometers through Sölden up to Hochgurgl. From South Tyrol, access is available in summer across the Timmelsjoch pass road. Regular VVT buses link Ötztal Bahnhof directly with Hochgurgl.

Tips

After touring the motorcycle collection, unwind on the wind-sheltered sun terrace at Top Mountain Crosspoint and sample wood-fired pizza or Tyrolean dishes. Continuing over the Timmelsjoch to explore the architectural stations of the "Timmelsjoch Experience" is an unforgettable road trip.
